faithful tensor model of Chow correspondences

outputs.exact_statement: Set $$g=10^{60},\qquad D_*=\binom g3,\qquad n=3D_*.$$ The explicitly defined class $Y\in S_{g,n}^{2D_*}$ of Definition 5 satisfies $$q_{g,n}(Y)=0,\qquad Y\notin\mathcal P_{g,n}.$$ Consequently Pixton’s original relation span does not exhaust the tautological Chow relations: the equality $\ker q_{g,n}=\mathcal P_{g,n}$ fails for this stable pair.

For the stable pair and class $Y$ of Theorem 1, $$q^H_{g,n}(Y)=0 \quad\text{in }H^{4D_*}\!\left(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}(\mathbb C);\mathbb Q\right), \qquad Y\notin\mathcal P_{g,n}.$$ In particular, $\mathcal P_{g,n}\subsetneq\ker q^H_{g,n}$.

The span in Definition 3 is an ideal and is stable under tautological gluing and forgetting pushforwards and pullbacks. For gluing pullback to a product, the target relation space is the sum of the spaces with a relation in one factor. Moreover $$\mathcal P_{g,n}\subseteq\ker q_{g,n}.$$

There are a supercommutative $\mathbb Q$-algebra $R$, a finite free supermodule $V$ over $R$, and $\mathbb Q$-linear maps $$t_m:S_{g,m}\longrightarrow V^{\otimes_R m}
 \qquad(m\geq 0)$$ such that $t_m(\mathcal P_{g,m})=0$ for every $m$, whereas $t_n(Y)\neq0$. In particular $Y\notin\mathcal P_{g,n}$.

These rules give a supercommutative associative Frobenius algebra. The product of three standard odd vectors belongs to $Re$, and the product of four such vectors is zero. Its handle element is $$\mu\Delta(1)=(2-2g)e.$$

The prescription is well defined modulo genuine relations on rational parameter factors and induces a map on $S_{g,m}$. For a homogeneous expression of degree $r$, its image is a sum of tensors indexed by partitions of the labels into nonempty blocks, of the form $$\bigotimes_{L}\Delta_L(\lambda^{d_L}),
 \qquad
 r=\sum_L\bigl(|L|-1+d_L\bigr).
 \label{eq:detector-blocks}$$ In particular $t_m$ is zero in degrees $r>m$.

For every strata expression $b$, the maps $t_m$ satisfy $$t(\pi_y^*b)=t(b)\otimes1,
 \qquad
 t(\pi_{y*}b)=\int_y t(b).
 \label{eq:detector-forget}$$ Here $\pi_y$ forgets the label $y$; the identities hold in any order of the remaining labels.

If all preceding leg indices $a_j$ are zero or one, then, in the untruncated rational-tails computation, $$\mathcal R(s;a,0)
 -\sum_\ell s_\ell\mathcal R(s;a,\ell)
 =\pi_y^*\mathcal R(s;a).
 \label{eq:detector-unit}$$
For every $m\geq0$, $t_m(\mathcal P_{g,m})=0$.

In the setup above, either in relative rational Chow or in the indicated quotient by base support, there is a supercommutative rational algebra $\mathfrak B$ with the following properties.*

1.  *The curve correspondence algebra has a faithful tensor model on $$\mathfrak B\otimes
     \bigl(\mathbb Q1\oplus W_b\oplus\mathbb Qe\bigr),$$ where $1,e$ are even and $W_b$ is an odd symplectic space of dimension $2b$. The classes $1_C,e'_C$ correspond to $1,e$, and $\eta$ projects onto $W_b$. Integration gives the hyperbolic pairing $\langle1,e\rangle=1$, $\langle1,1\rangle=\langle e,e\rangle=0$ on the two even summands and the symplectic pairing on $W_b$. All actual Chow correspondences between curve powers, not only pairing diagrams, are included faithfully in this model.*

2.  *The projected small diagonal is an alternating three-form $$\varphi\colon W_b^3\longrightarrow\mathfrak B_{\mathrm{odd}}.$$ Cup product, integration, tensor products, permutations, and contractions are computed in the model with the Koszul signs.*

3.  *Let $U$ be a finite-dimensional ordinary rational color space. A pure colored tensor in $$\label{eq:colored-chow-space}
     \left(
       \eta^{\otimes k}A^*(C^k)
       \otimes U^{\otimes k}\otimes\mathrm{sgn}_k
     \right)_{\mathfrak S_k}$$ is zero if and only if all its evaluations using the same ordinary linear map $z\colon U\to W_b$ in every slot are zero in $\mathfrak B$. Finitely many rational maps $z$ suffice for each fixed $U,k$. The assertion holds in the base-support quotient as well.*

*In particular, a product of projected cubic entries is tested by products of $\varphi(z(i),z(j),z(k))$, with the fixed Koszul sign coming from the ordering of the factors. A vanishing established by these tests is a vanishing in Chow, with the stated base-support bound.

Let $F$ be the functor in [eq:symplectic-chow-functor], and put $H(X)=\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal C}(1,F(X))$. There is a supercommutative $\mathop{\mathrm{Sp}}_{2b}$-algebra $\mathfrak B$ such that, naturally in $X$, $$\label{eq:coefficient-invariants} H(X)\simeq(\mathfrak B\otimes X)^{\mathop{\mathrm{Sp}}_{2b}}.$$ Under these identifications, tensor products of target morphisms become multiplication of coefficients. Arbitrary morphisms $F(X)\to F(Y)$ are represented faithfully by equivariant $\mathfrak B$-linear maps $\mathfrak B\otimes X\to\mathfrak B\otimes Y$, and their composition is the usual tensor contraction.

Work modulo positive-codimension base support, and suppose $e_C$ is the class of a section. Then $e'_C=e_C$ in the quotient. In the model of Proposition 13, the functional $$\epsilon(x)=\int_C e_Cx$$ is multiplicative and satisfies $$\epsilon(1)=1,\qquad \epsilon(e)=0,\qquad \epsilon(W_b)=0.$$ Consequently the component of a product $w_1w_2$, with $w_1,w_2\in W_b$, in the two even summands is $\langle w_1,w_2\rangle e$.

In the pure subspace $\eta^{\otimes k}\mathcal A_k(U)$, evaluations using the same scalar map $z\colon U\to W_b$ in every slot are jointly injective. For fixed $k,U$, a finite collection of rational maps is jointly injective. These statements hold after quotienting by base support of any prescribed positive codimension.

The derived stack of arrows with target $V$ has an open derived substack whose classical truncation is the ordinary relative Quot scheme with the prescribed Hilbert polynomial, before fixing determinant. On this truncation its relative tangent complex is $$\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(
 \mathbf R\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(I',I')\longrightarrow
 \mathbf R\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(I',V)\bigr)
 \simeq \mathbf R\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(I',Q).$$ This is a perfect complex of Tor-amplitude $[0,1]$, compatible with base change. The differential of forgetting the arrow and keeping its source is the boundary map $$\mathbf R\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(I',Q)\longrightarrow\mathbf R\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(I',I')[1].$$

Let $0\to F\to V_0\to Q_0\to0$ be an exact sequence on a smooth projective surface, where $V_0$ is a vector bundle of rank $r$ and $Q_0$ is torsion. If $K$ is ample and $Kc_1(Q_0)>rK^2$, the map $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^1(F,Q_0)\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^2(F,F)
 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}}H^2(\mathcal O_X)$$ is surjective.

Fix finitely many marked output surface factors. Push forward, over relative point Hilbert schemes and any additional surface factors, a finite polynomial in Chern characters of universal point ideals, their derived duals, line classes, relative tangent Chern classes, and equality diagonals. The resulting Chow class is a universal finite sum of decorated equality diagonals among the outputs, multiplied by relative characteristic pushes from closed surface components. One fixed polynomial procedure chooses the expression, independently of the surface family. No marked output is integrated in the procedure.
Under the hypotheses of Theorem 18, the scalar $a_{N,t_0}$ satisfies $$a_{N,t_0}\,T_\gamma^{\,t_0}=0 \qquad\text{in }\mathfrak B_{S,b-1}.$$
The bare-triple scalar $a_{N,t_0}$ in Proposition 23 is nonzero. Consequently Theorem 18 holds.

Let $F\subset H$ be vector spaces of dimensions $2r$ and $D$, and let $\Omega\in\bigwedge^2F$ be nondegenerate. If $0\le t\le r$, then the ideal generated by $\Omega^t$ in $\bigwedge H$ contains $\bigwedge^qH$ for every $q\ge D-r+t$.

Let a smooth curve family of genus $b\ge5$, with a section, be over a smooth irreducible quasi-projective base $S$ satisfying $\dim S<(b-1)^2-1$. Put $$t_b=25(b-1)^2-1.$$ Let $E$ be an $m$-dimensional color space, and let $e$ be an even integer with $e\ge m/2-2$ and $e\le m/2$. Write $D_E=\binom m3$ and $d_e=\binom e3$. If $t_b\le d_e/2$, every product of $$q\ge D_E-d_e/2+t_b$$ pure cubic entries whose colors lie in $E$ vanishes modulo support in base codimension at least $b-1$.

Let $g\geq2$, let the heavy set be empty, and pull the three-light operations to any larger number of light labels by forgetting. Under weight reduction from ordinary stable pointed curves, $[i=j]$ pulls back to $\bar D_{ij}$ and $\beta_{g,\varnothing}$ pulls back to the normalized two-edge bridge sum used to define $\beta_J^{\mathrm{st}}$. Consequently the coefficient of the prescribed color word in the signed product of all $F^0_{g,\varnothing}$ pulls back to $q(Y)$, up to a nonzero rational scalar.

The map [eq:coarse-positions] is the iterated blowup obtained, at each flag $p$, by first blowing up the locus where all three assigned positions equal $p$, when present, and then the strict transforms of the loci where two assigned positions equal $p$. The latter centers are disjoint after the first blowup.
For the pullback of a raw cubic class $F^0$ from an ancestor chart, the coefficient $a_p$ in [eq:blowup-components] is zero at every triple flag locus.

For every stable heavy type $(h,B)$ one can choose a symmetric class $G_{h,B}\in A^2(X_{h,B}(3))$ with the following properties.* 1. *Over the smooth heavy base, $G_{h,B}$ is exactly the pullback of $\Delta_C^{\mathrm{pure}}$ by the coarse-position map.* 2. *Pull a raw cubic $F^0$, or one of these chosen pure lifts $G$, from any ancestor chart to a compact descendant cut chart. Its operation is a sum of the chosen pure lifts at the relevant descendant vertices, with all three labels assigned to that vertex, together with pair-times-singleton operations and a residual cubic operation.* 3. *The singleton operations in (ii), and all their further pullbacks through cuts and light forgetting, are controlled as follows. Over fixed smooth core data their restrictions lie componentwise in the span of the unit, the canonical class, and the flag points. On any smooth test family the same statement holds modulo classes supported over positive base codimension.* 4. *On the current smooth-core open the residual operation in (ii) is a finite sum of classes containing a pulled base divisor factor. The base divisor may come from the current heavy base or from a compact ancestor base. Consequently its pullback to every smooth test family is zero operationally after removing a positive-codimension subset of that test base.* *All expansions preserve the color multiset. They may always use one and the same chosen $G$ and centering at a given current vertex, regardless of which ancestor supplied the operation.

Let a cycle multiplier on $X^\Gamma(n)$ have base image contained in an irreducible closed subspace $Z\subset\mathcal B_\Gamma$. After passing to a refinement if necessary, suppose that its generic base image lies in $\mathcal S_\Gamma$. Let $L$ be a factor involving a specified subset of the active entries.*

*Suppose that the pull of $L$ vanishes operationally over a dense open of a smooth test family dominating $Z\cap\mathcal S_\Gamma$. Then its action can be written as a finite sum of cycles with strictly smaller base-image dimension. Only the entries in $L$ are consumed.*

*More precisely, take a smooth test base $S$, proper and generically finite over $Z\cap\mathcal S_\Gamma$. If the vanishing holds off base codimension at least $a$, the terms remaining over $\mathcal S_\Gamma$ have base-image dimension at most $\dim Z-a$. The other terms lie over $Z\setminus\mathcal S_\Gamma$ and require a strict graph refinement. If one first replaces $S$ by the total space of one of its curve families to obtain a section, the corresponding bound is $\dim Z-a+1$.

Set $$R_\Gamma=2|V(\Gamma)|+2|E(\Gamma)|.$$ If $R_\Gamma+1$ noise entries have their singleton at the same color, their product advances support while consuming those entries. If a genus-$h$ vertex has more than $\binom{2h}{3}$ pure entries, the product of any $\binom{2h}{3}+1$ of them advances support.

Suppose that a vertex of genus $h$ has a flag and that $k>\binom{h+1}{2}$ pure entries contain one common color $i$. Their product is a finite linear combination of products $L*H$ with the following properties:*

1.  *$L$ involves at most $h+2$ entries and vanishes modulo positive base support;*

2.  *$H$ is still a product of individual pure entries at that vertex;*

3.  *before removing the entries in $L$, each term has the same color multiset as the original product.*

*Consequently each term admits a support advancement consuming at most $h+2$ entries.

The class $Y\in S_{g,n}$ constructed above satisfies $$q_{g,n}(Y)=0
 \quad\text{in }A^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n};\mathbb Q).$$

purpose: A high-arity counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow

coverage.checked_domain: A in 0..3, B in 0..3, n in 0..6; exact coefficient values only, not the full parameters with chi at least 16
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent closed-form binomial sum plus exact comparison with hand-computed expected values; positivity is not decided beyond the tested domain.

title: A high-arity counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow
